route: Official WordPress.com ChatGPT plugin or Claude connector, backed by WordPress.com hosted MCP
read: Posts, pages, blocks, site settings and statistics within enabled tools and the user's site permissions.

write.draft: Yes. New posts and pages default to draft.
write.edit: Yes. Whole content or individual block sections; published content can change immediately.
write.publish: Yes. Post/page status changes can publish content.
write.delete: Yes. Posts/pages move to trash; documented restoration window is 30 days. Other object deletion semantics vary.

setupDetails: Enable MCP, connect the native ChatGPT plugin or Claude connector, and authorise via OAuth. No separate server installation. Configure account/site tool access.
access: All WordPress.com paid plans. Free sites temporarily included through 30 November 2026. Jetpack-connected sites use the same server; developer docs identify Jetpack AI or Complete after the temporary no-plan period.
limitations: Access is limited by user roles and enabled tools.
Read/write groups are enabled when MCP is switched on; review access rather than assuming read-only defaults.
Connected clients share WordPress.com account/site tool settings.
Updating live content is not necessarily a staged draft workflow.

changedClaims: B+ to A under the read/write/setup rubric.

route: Official WordPress MCP Adapter plugin exposing installed WordPress Abilities
read: Depends on installed, publicly exposed abilities. Adapter discovery is not evidence that posts/pages are readable.

write.draft: Depends on an installed editorial ability.
write.edit: Depends on installed abilities and permissions.
write.publish: Depends on an explicit publication ability or supported status operation.
write.delete: Depends on an explicit deletion ability; not supplied merely by installing the adapter.

setupDetails: Install the WordPress MCP Adapter plugin on the site; configure authenticated HTTP or WP-CLI STDIO access and supply/expose the required abilities. Remote examples use a local proxy and application password.
access: Site administration and compatible WordPress/Abilities versions. Abilities are private by default and require public metadata; each ability has its own permission checks.
limitations: An integration framework, not a complete out-of-the-box editorial assistant.
Do not inherit the WordPress.com hosted service's capabilities or installed third-party abilities.
Verify discovery and schemas on the target installation before claiming a specific workflow.

changedClaims: B to C when grading usable marketing workflows and setup, rather than infrastructure potential.

route: Official Webflow ChatGPT app or Claude connector backed by hosted Webflow MCP
read: Collections, schemas, CMS items and site data; the same MCP also covers many design operations.

write.draft: Yes. CMS item creation is staged as drafts.
write.edit: Yes. CMS item updates are drafts; collection fields and many design properties are also editable.
write.publish: Yes. Explicit publish and unpublish collection item actions.
write.delete: Yes. Explicit collection item and collection field deletion actions.

setupDetails: Connect the ChatGPT app or Claude connector and authorise sites through OAuth. The bridge is installed automatically; no self-hosted server is required.
access: Existing accessible Webflow site, user permissions and one workspace per authorisation. Enterprise is required for the page-branch lifecycle, not ordinary CMS item operations.
limitations: Cannot create new site projects.
Cannot create new localised CMS items; existing secondary-locale items can be read/updated.
Visual snapshots, image uploads and current Designer selection/context operations require the Designer and bridge open; routine CMS operations do not.
Campaigns early access cannot launch advertising assets from MCP.

changedClaims: B+ to A-.

route: Official Contentful-hosted remote MCP with OAuth and per-environment MCP app configuration
read: Entries, schemas, assets, references, snapshots, locales and releases.

write.edit: Yes. Entries, assets, models and locales.
write.publish: Yes. Entry/asset publication and unpublication; release validation, immediate publication and scheduled publication/unpublication are documented.
write.delete: Yes. Explicit entry, asset, content-model and locale deletion tools.

setupDetails: Add the global or EU hosted URL to an MCP client, authenticate with OAuth, install/configure the MCP app in each target space/environment and enable the required tools.
access: User permissions plus per-space/environment allowlists. Local PAT alternative exists but has a different, broader access model.
limitations: The app must be configured for each target environment.
Local SPACE_ID/ENVIRONMENT_ID values are context defaults, not security boundaries.
Publishing CMS data does not by itself establish that a separately hosted frontend has deployed or refreshed.

sources.label: Hosted/local setup, permissions, regions and full tool table

gradeReason: Broad content lifecycle and release operations without hosting a bridge, with a small administrator configuration step.
changedClaims: Keep A-.
Keep remote and local PAT access boundaries explicit.
Include EU hosted endpoint option; do not call the Contentful configuration app a native ChatGPT/Claude marketplace app.

route: Official hosted Sanity MCP at mcp.sanity.io; distinct from read-only Sanity Context MCP
read: GROQ document queries, exact document lookup, schema and project/dataset context.

write.draft: Yes. Document creation normally produces drafts; liveEdit types create published documents; release versions are also supported.
write.edit: Yes. Patches target drafts or release versions.
write.publish: Yes for individual drafts; unpublish is explicit. Creating/listing releases and adding versions is supported, but scheduling/publishing/archiving/deleting releases is not available through the current release tools.
write.delete: Partial. Discard drafts and release versions; no general published-document deletion tool verified.

setupDetails: Connect an MCP-capable client via hosted URL and OAuth, or use the Sanity CLI to configure a supported coding client. Token authentication is an alternative.
access: Sanity account with project/dataset permissions. Available tools can vary. Deployed schemas enable validation before writes.
limitations: Release lifecycle actions beyond creation/listing/version changes require Studio or the HTTP Actions API.
Context MCP is a separate read-only server and cannot inherit these write claims.
liveEdit document types have different draft semantics.
General published-document deletion remains unverified.

gradeReason: Broad routine content authoring and publication with a hosted connection; explicit limits prevent a full A.
changedClaims: Keep A- but make release scheduling/publication limits prominent.
Do not describe all content release management as automated.
Keep delete partial rather than inferred from underlying APIs.

route: Built-in remote MCP served by the existing Directus instance
read: Collection items, schema, fields, relationships, files and automation context within user permissions.

write.draft: Schema-dependent. Create items with the project's draft/status conventions.
write.edit: Yes. Item CRUD, files, schema and automation tools.
write.publish: Schema/workflow-dependent. There is no universal CMS publish operation across every Directus project.
write.delete: Yes when both user permissions and the Allow Deletes setting permit it; global deletion is off by default.

setupDetails: For an existing hosted instance, enable MCP and connect its /mcp URL. OAuth is now documented; self-hosted instances need OAuth environment settings, registration configuration and a restart. Static tokens remain an alternative.
access: MCP requires Directus 11.12+. Actual instance version, administrator enablement and user permissions govern available tools. Self-hosted operation belongs in the self-managed tier when infrastructure must be maintained by the user.
limitations: Draft, publishing and localisation depend on the project's data model.
OAuth availability must be checked against the deployed version/configuration, not inferred from the 11.12 minimum alone.
Registry mode funnels actions through execute and reduces per-tool client approval granularity.

route: Official Shopify AI Toolkit plugin plus authenticated Shopify CLI store commands using Admin GraphQL
read: Authenticated Admin GraphQL queries, including paginated online-store pages. Granted scopes limit accessible resources.

write.draft: Yes. Page creation supports unpublished state; articles have publication controls.
write.edit: Yes. Page content, handles, templates and publication settings can be updated.
write.publish: Yes. Page publication controls and article immediate/scheduled publication are documented.
write.delete: Yes. Explicit pageDelete and articleDelete mutations permanently delete content.

setupDetails: Install the official AI Toolkit plugin in a supported coding agent, provide Node.js/CLI prerequisites, authorise the app/store with required Admin API scopes, then execute prepared queries. Mutations require explicit --allow-mutations.
access: Supported coding-agent clients and authenticated store/app context. Content writes require write_content or write_online_store_pages. This is not the consumer shopping MCP or a generic ChatGPT merchant-admin app.
limitations: Plugin installation alone does not authorise store writes.
CLI/runtime and scoped store authentication are still required.
No native ChatGPT/Claude browser-app merchant CMS route established by this evidence.
The toolkit's developer-docs MCP is distinct from CLI-authenticated store execution.

route: Official WooCommerce abilities through the separately installed WordPress MCP Adapter
read: Product queries; order queries and order notes within permissions.

write.draft: Review pending for the currently installed product ability schema; creation alone does not establish safe draft defaults.
write.edit: Yes. Product creation/update; bounded order status and note operations.
write.publish: Review pending for the current product status schema; do not infer a dedicated publication workflow.
write.delete: Yes. Purpose-built product deletion ability documented.

setupDetails: Install/activate the MCP Adapter, use a dedicated WordPress user and application password, and configure the official remote proxy or local WP-CLI STDIO connection. Verify discovered abilities and schemas.
access: Developer preview. WooCommerce registers abilities; each checks permissions. HTTPS and suitable permalink settings are needed for the remote route.
limitations: WooCommerce 11.3 removes /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp and its WooCommerce REST API key authentication.
Core no longer bundles the adapter.
Legacy/custom abilities do not automatically carry over; public exposure metadata matters.
Editorial draft/publication and localisation depend on the installed schemas/extensions.

route: Official early-access Store Management MCP for product content; page/blog Content APIs remain a separate custom route
read: Product detail/search and selected store, order, inventory and promotion data. No CMS page/blog read tools established in the Management MCP tool list.

write.draft: Partial. Products are created hidden. This is not a generic CMS page/blog draft workflow.
write.edit: Yes for product copy, SEO fields and selected commerce data. Page/blog editing is outside the documented MCP tool list.
write.publish: No product visibility/publish tool documented; hidden products require review/publication elsewhere. Promotions start disabled.
write.delete: No product/page/blog deletion tool in the documented Management MCP tool list.

setupDetails: Store owner enables early access and accepts terms, grants scopes to the connecting user, then adds the hosted URL as a custom MCP connector and completes OAuth.
access: Active store, owner enablement, explicit per-user/per-store grants. New users start with no scopes. Rate limits depend on store plan.
limitations: Early access, not the GA Storefront MCP.
Storefront MCP acts as a shopper; its capabilities must not be assigned to merchant administration.
Current tool list covers catalog operations but not page/blog CMS lifecycle.
Same user's connected agents share scope grants.

route: Traditional Adobe Commerce/Magento CMS REST API via a custom agent integration
read: CMS pages and blocks via read/search endpoints.

write.draft: Partial. Inactive content can be represented, but no general editorial draft/approval system is established by these APIs.
write.edit: Yes. CMS page/block create and update endpoints.
write.publish: Partial. Page is_active controls availability; visual Page Builder validation and a full release workflow are not established.
write.delete: Yes. CMS page/block delete endpoints, subject to CMS permissions.

setupDetails: A developer configures a scoped Commerce integration and implements the assistant/API connection, including store-view targeting and publication checks.
access: Traditional Commerce PaaS/on-premises/Magento API scope. Adobe explicitly documents materially different SaaS endpoint availability.
limitations: No ready official external-agent CMS connector established in this research.
Do not generalise to Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service.
Structured content API access is not proof of correct visual Page Builder editing.
No universal editorial review/approval workflow inferred.
